author: William Crooks
title: SQ warns of fake representative fraud surge in Val-Saint-François and Des Sources
text:
Get local news like this every morning. Subscribe free below.
Pulse Newsroom
The Sûreté du Québec is warning residents in the Val-Saint-François and Des Sources regional county municipalities after more than a dozen reports of so-called “fake representative” fraud were received within a 24-hour period.
Some of the reported incidents resulted in financial losses, according to a public warning issued by the SQ’s Estrie/Centre-du-Québec region.
Police said the scheme generally begins with a telephone call from someone pretending to be a police officer, an Equifax employee or a representative of a financial institution.
The caller tells the intended victim that they have been targeted by fraud or are connected to an ongoing investigation. The fraudster then attempts to obtain personal or financial information, claiming it is necessary to “verify” or resolve the situation.
In several cases, police said, the fraudster was already in possession of some of the victim’s personal information.
The scheme can go further than requesting information over the phone. According to the SQ, fraudsters may instruct victims to place their bank cards in an envelope or prepare cash so that someone can come to their home and collect it.
Police described fake representative fraud as a growing problem in Quebec that deliberately targets vulnerable seniors.
The SQ is urging residents never to provide personal or banking information over the telephone.
Police officers, financial institution representatives and agency employees will not ask people to provide their PIN, bank cards, jewellery or cash, the SQ said.
Anyone who receives a suspicious call should hang up. The SQ recommends contacting 911 or calling the financial institution directly if there is any doubt about whether a request is legitimate.
People who believe they have been targeted are encouraged to report the incident to the Sûreté du Québec and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre at 1-888-495-8501.
Reports of cybercrime and fraud can also be submitted through the federal government’s national online reporting system.
The SQ said reporting attempted fraud is important even when no money has been lost, as each report can contribute to efforts to combat fraudulent schemes.
Police are asking residents throughout the affected communities to remain vigilant as the recent series of incidents continues to be investigated.
